findings.actual: ObserveInvalidatedPublicSlot receives the slot object but passes only the actor ID to ObserveNativeSlotInvalidated. That marks the previously sampled entry interrupted. If the rider moved the control from 9 to 3 since the last update, cleanup of slot 3 makes reconciliation restore slot 9. With no previous entry, the notification records nothing.
findings.blocking_rationale: Native cleanup can undo a deliberate move or erase a newly placed shortcut.
findings.expected: When native cleanup invalidates the public control, the recoverable index is the slot that actually held it.
findings.requested_correction: Identify the exact slot on the current rider’s bar while it is still observable and retain that index. Ignore invalidated slot objects that do not belong to that bar.
findings.requested_evidence: Move 9 to 3, invalidate and clear 3, then reactivate before reconciliation. Verify one binding at 3 and none at 9. Repeat for a first manual placement and retain the continuous-fact manual-removal control.
findings.title: Native invalidation remembers the last sampled index instead of the invalidated slot
findings.trigger: The player places or moves Mount / Dismount and native bad-slot cleanup runs before the next control update.

findings.actual: ObserveArrangementOnBar finds the slot by blueprint and marks it bound. ClassifyArrangementsForCapture then exits for an active replacement fact. CaptureLiveSlots skips the slot because its old AbilityData fails the reference-equality check. TryGetArrangement also skips it because the entry is marked continuously bound. Only the placement marker can remain, which loads as an off-bar choice.
findings.blocking_rationale: The live session can repair the binding on its next update while a cold load of the same save loses it.
findings.expected: A stale binding to the right public blueprint preserves the player’s slot as an archive index. Restore binds the current fact.
findings.requested_correction: Base header classification on whether the live writer can emit this specific binding. Carry the observed index as placement intent when the binding needs repair, while retaining the live-fact and caster checks on callable data.
findings.requested_evidence: Use distinct old and new AbilityData objects for the same public blueprint. Save with the old data in slot 9 and the replacement fact active, before reconciliation. Decode one kind-6 row at 9 and one kind-7 record, then cold-restore once to the new data. A deliberate removal must still produce only kind 7.
findings.title: An active replacement fact can make the save header omit a stale but recoverable slot
findings.trigger: The save header runs after the fact has been replaced but before ReconcilePublicControlSlots has rebound the old slot data.

findings.actual: Header classification and live capture both enumerate only current candidates. A newly remote rider is absent from both. RevalidateAbsentArrangements can confirm its pet link, but does not observe its bar or mark the departure. TryGetArrangement consequently refuses its last continuously bound index. The later save scope can clear the old bar through observedUnits after the archive is already fixed.
findings.blocking_rationale: A city save can omit both the chosen slot and its placement record. Loading it can trigger automatic placement in a different slot.
findings.expected: The first reserve save contains the departing rider’s final arrangement regardless of whether the regular departure loop has run.
findings.requested_correction: Handle still-observed riders that have left the candidate roster at the save barrier. Observe their last bar and classify temporary versus permanent departure before emitting rows, with exact-world and replacement-object checks.
findings.requested_evidence: Change just the native roster membership, then capture the header before running ReconcileFacts. Verify an unchanged slot 9, a move to 3, and a deliberate removal through archive capture and cold return. The fixture must allow roster mutation and departure reconciliation to occur separately.
findings.title: A reserve save before departure reconciliation omits the rider’s last arrangement
findings.trigger: A dismounted rider leaves PartyCharacters for RemoteCompanions and the save header runs before the next toolbar update.

findings.actual: BeginLoadedWorld clears the intent map but retains observedUnits. The departure loop can then read an outgoing object’s bar into the cleared map. Its presentNow guard searches current candidates only. A same-ID rider in the incoming reserve roster fails that guard but passes IsStillOnPlayerRoster by ID. The outgoing slot can thus become a temporary arrangement in the incoming world, including when the selected save has no slot row for that rider.
findings.blocking_rationale: Loading a different save from the same campaign can import a toolbar choice from the session being discarded.
findings.expected: After load begins, cleanup of old objects cannot author placement intent for an actor in the incoming world.
findings.requested_correction: Separate outgoing-object cleanup from current-world arrangement observation. Bind departure observations to the owning world and exact roster instance, including reserve riders.
findings.requested_evidence: Use one service across two player worlds with distinct rider objects sharing an actor ID. Leave slot 9 bound in the outgoing world and load a save with the rider in reserve and no slot row. Verify that saving again or returning the rider to the party never reproduces the outgoing choice. Repeat with an explicit off-bar record.
findings.title: An outgoing rider can repopulate placement intent after a load clears it
findings.trigger: A load replaces a previously observed party rider with a reserve instance of the same actor.

findings.expected: The remaining area-adapter failure is classified by one matched base and candidate diagnostic comparison.
findings.requested_correction: Run the isolated area adapter once on the fixed base under the same compiler and inputs. Compare its diagnostics with the candidate and update the handoff with the observed differences. A matching pre-existing failure can remain documented.
findings.requested_evidence: Provide source identities, invocation, exits and normalized compiler diagnostics for both trees, or a passing candidate adapter result exercising the in-world restore assertion.
findings.title: The area-adapter baseline failure has no matched baseline run
findings.trigger: The handoff attributes the excluded area preflight adapter’s remaining compile errors to the base tree.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: The IsBad postfix covers the previously sampled slot-9 case, including reactivation before an update. It discards the actual slot identity, so a more recent placement or move still fails under the same cleanup.

The focused gate now includes the production archive validator and codec. The test compares decoded actor IDs, indices and kinds across all 128 rows, requires the specific bound refusal at 129, and round-trips a marker-only arrangement.
Header classification handles the tested empty-slot invalidation. It still loses an observed binding when an active replacement fact has different AbilityData from the slot.
The regular departure loop now observes the bar before clearing it. A header between the roster change and that loop still skips the rider. The test double makes those two events inseparable.

For a reconciled rider with no live lease, the decision now revalidates PetUniqueId. An unresolved pet with the same link keeps its arrangement, and a cleared link retires it. Both cases appear in the selected component regression.

Successful lease release records ObserveBound immediately after replacing the exact placeholder with the active public fact. The regression removes the restored control before another update and checks the marker-only save and load.

The candidate corrects both facade signatures and exercises archive capture and loaded-world restore in the six-pair adapter. The in-world assertion remains unexecuted, and the requested matched base diagnostic was replaced by source inspection.

summary.delivered_behavior: The candidate records per-rider toolbar intent using existing archive rows, projects eligible reserve owners’ persistent pets into the capital’s native UI roster, and carries an explicit mounted attack order on a living enemy that was already unconscious. The two city reports share a roster transition as a trigger. Their identified causes are distinct.
